about.lead: Hi, I'm Walaa. I'm a web developer based in Paris, with a background in computer science and a passion for building things that are both beautiful and technically solid.
about.p1: I enjoy working at the intersection of design and development - turning an idea or a business into a polished website that feels intentional on every screen.
about.p2: Alongside web development, I was selected for a supervised university research project in cryptography, where I studied RSA and real-world security. It taught me to approach technical problems with curiosity, precision and attention to detail - a mindset I bring to every website I build.

p1.title: Mirasens - A website designed to answer visitors, not just look good
p1.body: A multilingual (FR/EN) production website with a live AI assistant, built to help visitors get answers without waiting on a reply from the team.
p1.challengeBody: The business needed a fast, bilingual site that could answer visitor questions instantly - without a support team on standby.
p1.approachBody: Designed and built the site, set up FR/EN structure and SEO, then integrated an AI assistant to handle real visitor questions live.
p1.resultBody: A production website launched for real users, running live at mirasens.com today.

p2.title: Le Pacha - Restaurant Website & Custom CMS
p2.body: A real one-page website built for a real client - Le Pacha, a Turkish restaurant in Villejuif - with SEO, a reservation call-to-action, and a custom admin panel so the owner can update the menu and opening hours themselves.
p2.challengeBody: The owner needed a professional site to be found on Google locally and showcase the menu, but couldn't afford a developer every time a dish or price changed.
p2.approachBody: Designed and built a responsive one-page site (hero, menu highlights, gallery, hours, contact) optimized for local SEO, then built a custom CMS/admin panel from scratch so the client can add, edit or remove menu items, prices and categories, and update opening hours, with no coding needed.
p2.resultBody: Delivered end-to-end as an independent freelance project, live in production and used daily by a real restaurant owner.

researchModal.kicker: Initiation to Research · L1 Computer Science
researchModal.title: The RSA Cryptosystem
researchModal.subtitle: Mathematical Foundations and Security Analysis
researchModal.abstract: This project studies the RSA cryptosystem (Rivest, Shamir, Adleman, 1978), one of the most influential public-key algorithms in the history of computer security. After introducing classical and modern cryptography - substitution and stream ciphers, symmetric AES encryption, Diffie-Hellman key exchange and hash functions - it builds the mathematical toolkit behind RSA: modular arithmetic, the extended Euclidean algorithm, Euler's totient function, Euler's theorem, the Chinese remainder theorem and fast modular exponentiation. It then details RSA end to end: key generation, encryption, decryption, digital signatures and the RSA-CRT optimization. A dedicated security analysis studies integer factorization (Pollard's rho, the quadratic sieve, the general number field sieve) and several concrete attacks - the common modulus attack, the blinding attack exploiting RSA's multiplicative homomorphism, and Bleichenbacher's attack on PKCS#1 padding, which recovers a message after roughly 10⁶ queries and once compromised SSL/TLS in practice.
researchModal.plan5sub: RSA vs. post-quantum · Dropped in TLS 1.3
